## 1. BAR rule (rng_20, true-range bars), every constant
Code: `outputs/code/th_bars/kernels.py` k_range lines 34-57; box `outputs/code/th_bars/build_month.py` line 107 (`k_range(..., np.maximum(1, np.round(p * S['rng'])) ...)` with p = 20, S['rng'] = s_rng of the print's td); scales() lines 13-32; sessions `common.py` lines 10-17 (ET: code 0 Asia 18:00-02:00, 1 London 02:00-08:30, 2 pre 08:30-09:30, 3 NY AM 09:30-12:00, 4 NY PM 12:00-16:00, 5 close 16:00-18:00; td = ET + 6 h; session id td x 10 + code).
1. Input = every trade record, unmerged (run merge does not change these bars).
2. BOX B = max(1, round(20 x s_rng)) ticks of 0.25 point (numpy half-to-even), fixed for the whole td. s_rng = trailing median of the 20 previous stats_day range rows / 191.5 (D8_ASIA_NEWBOOK_INPUTS.md sections 2-3). td 20261027: s_rng 2.189948 -> B = 44 ticks = 11.00 points; td 20261110: s_rng 3.048303 -> B = 61 ticks = 15.25 points (engine store as it is; hole-filled alternative: 65 ticks on 20261110, section 4).
3. State per (session key, instrument id): at a change of key or instrument id the open bar is emitted with part = 1 (known at its last print) and the series restarts at bar index 0 (lines 40-43).
4. A bar opens at the first print after the previous bar closed (or the session's first print): o = h = l = c = p, volume 0.
5. For each later print p: if the bar is open and max(h, p) - min(l, p) > B (STRICTLY greater than B ticks), the bar CLOSES BEFORE this print: it is emitted with the prints already in it (o, h, l, c of the previous prints, volume, t1 = last included print), known time = timestamp (ts_event) of THIS breaching print; the breaching print opens the NEXT bar (it is not part of the closing bar) (lines 45-48).
6. Otherwise the print is added: h/l/c updated, volume += size, n += 1, delta += side x size.
7. At the session end the open bar is emitted with part = 1 (known at the last print of the session, e.g. 13:29:59.810Z on 20261110): never a signal bar.
8. Series seen by the trigger: ALL sessions of all history concatenated in known-time order (D8_BAR_DEFS.md section 2). Bar counts: London td 20261027 361 bars (360 + 1 truncated), td 20261110 322 (321 + 1 truncated). First bar t0: 06:00:00.000Z (20261027) and 07:00:00.142Z (20261110, first London print).

## 2. TRIGGER rule (every constant)
Code: `outputs/code/th_grid/trig_book_imb.py` (shim) -> `outputs/code/th_grid/triggers_c/defs.py` lines 39-51 (spec book_imb: grid, `_imb`), `core.py` lines 31-49 (feature alignment), 63-67 (ema), 75-76 (edge), 78-85 (native_len), 87-101 (Ctx), 103-123 (emit), 125-136 (thr_signal), 138-146 (make); the feature: `triggers_c/featc.py` lines 87-96 (`grid_feats`: valid, imb) and 271-290 (`day_features`: snapshot lookup). Variant `follow_native`: sign +1 (follow), native; params lv = 1, thr = 0.35, sm = 60 (seconds).
1. FEATURE x = b_imb1 at each bar close = (bid1_size - ask1_size) / (bid1_size + ask1_size), the best-bid and best-ask sizes (contracts) of the order book, in [-1, +1]. Source = the mbp-10 book stream (CME MDP via the engine's Databento-style history): the snapshot is the book state after the LAST record of a 100-ms bucket (bucket = ts_recv // 100,000,000 ns), stamped with that record's ts_recv. A snapshot is VALID if bid1 price > 0, ask1 price > bid1 price (uncrossed) and both level-1 sizes > 0. For a bar known at T: take the last VALID snapshot with ts_recv <= T (invalid / crossed snapshots are skipped back to the previous valid one). The stored feature is rounded to float16.
2. SMOOTHING: sm = 60 clock seconds is converted to bars with the median seconds-per-bar of the FIRST 2,000 bars of the series (native_len): 29.24 s per bar -> sm = round(60 / 29.24) = 2 bars. xs = EMA of x with span 2 (pandas ewm(span = 2, adjust = False, ignore_na = True): alpha = 2/3, xs_0 = x_0, xs_j = (2/3) x_j + (1/3) xs_{j-1}); a NaN feature (no matching stored row: 947 of 1,401,032 bars) gives NaN and does not update the state.
3. LEVEL: long level = xs >= 0.35, short level = xs <= -0.35 (inclusive). EVENT = EDGE: long when the long level is true now and was not true on the previous bar (short mirrored). A bar that is both is dropped. `follow` = trade in the direction of the imbalance (bid-heavy = long).
4. WARM-UP: for a PRICE-family bar (rng is price family) native variants emit nothing before bar index 2,000 of the series; part = 1 bars never signal. Irrelevant live (history since 2023).
5. THE BOOK TRADES LONG ONLY: short events exist (82,990 in the raw history) and are discarded by the cell mode `long`. Do not code the short side.
6. Warm-up for a coder: the EMA span 2 forgets quickly (1/3 per bar): 20 prior bars are enough to match to the 1e-9 level; seed with the xs value printed in the first INPUTS row of each day.
7. DATA NEEDED beyond NQ trades: level-1 bid/ask size from the book feed with the 100-ms-final snapshot rule of item 1. The engine uses a replica of the book stream; whether an NT8 L1/L2 callback gives the same sizes at the same instants is NOT verified (open point 2).

## 3. From signal to order, sides, bracket, one position
`outputs/code/th_brkt/brkt_build.py` raw_events lines 34-42, make lines 43-48: keep a signal only if its bar has part == 0 and session code == 1 (London) (lines 38-39); order time ts = floor(bar known time to whole seconds) + 2 s (line 42); exit_ts = 08:30 ET (the end of the signal bar's ET session; 12:30Z in EDT, 13:30Z in EST); events with ts >= exit_ts dropped (a signal on a bar known after 08:29:58 ET never trades); LONG only (line 47); BRACKET shape P45: STOP 45.0 points and TARGET 45.0 points from the fill, fixed, 1 lot (1 point = 4 ticks = $20: 180 ticks = $900 each side per contract); cap_exit (th_fakefill/cap_exit.py): if no print follows the scheduled exit within 120 s the exit is the last print before it. Verified: my independent implementation of the whole chain on the stored bars and stored feature gives 9,988 events identical in time to the stored file; the engine's own raw_events + make gives the stored file exactly (ts, side, stop, target, exit, lots).
ONE POSITION per book: an event while the book is in a trade / exit pending / entry in flight is dropped (D8_BUILD_SPEC.md (b2)); the events file is not a trade list. Seen: 20261027 has 10 events and 8 trades: the 10:46:42Z and 10:48:26Z events fall inside open trades and are skipped. Session window: London bars (02:00-08:30 ET); flat at 08:30 ET (UWTime exit executed +1.0 s). Entry/fill/exit mechanics (quoted from D8_BUILD_SPEC.md (b2), not re-derived): market order at ts, fill 1.0 s later walking the 10-level book; stop order at fill - 45, target limit at fill + 45. Consistency on 20261027: every entry = order time + 1.000 s; seven of eight trades hit target (+45.00) or the stop (-42.75, 2.25 points better than 45: engine fill mechanics), the eighth ran to the session end (UWTime 12:30:01.000Z, +3.5 points).
